findings.reason: Confirmed in every part, with one numerical correction that does not touch the finding. The three mismatches are exactly as described: LD.0's description reads '**Inputs.** `FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.0`' with `requires` the empty list; LD.1 reads '**Inputs.** `LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.0`, `FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.4`' with `requires` holding only LD.0; LD.2 reads '**Inputs.** `LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.1`, `FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.2`' with `requires` holding only LD.1. The convention claim also holds, and it is what makes these anomalies rather than style: LD.3's prose Inputs are LD.2, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1 and MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.4, and its `requires` holds all three. FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration is indeed absent from the atlas — no file in research/blueprint/atlas/roadmaps/, none in research/blueprint/roadmaps/, and the string does not occur in research/blueprint/atlas/index.json — while its document does exist, at content/campaign/FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration/README.md. So the base layer of this roadmap has one declared input, that input cannot be resolved, and because `requires` is empty the atlas graph shows LD.0 with no prerequisites at all. Medium severity is right. Correction to the evidence, recorded because the numbers are offered as evidence: I count the roadmap cited **39** times by **23** other roadmap files (42 times across 24 files if the subject roadmap's own three mentions are included), where the finding says 41 times by 23 roadmaps. The roadmap count matches; the citation count is off by two. This does not bear on the claim, which rests on the absence of an atlas record rather than on how widely the missing roadmap is cited. The fix is correctly split into the part that belongs to this area (add the named inputs to the three `requires` fields once they resolve) and the part that does not (giving FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration an atlas record, which belongs to whoever owns the atlas build). A fix job raised from this finding should not be expected to complete the first half before the second exists.

Confirmed, and the library evidence is exact to the line. LD.0's text reads, verbatim: '... integrate model-theory foundations from Mathlib where available. Construct ultraproducts and prove the needed Los transfer theorem; nonstandard arithmetic uses an explicit elementary extension ...'. Mathlib/ModelTheory/Ultraproducts.lean is headed '# Ultraproducts and Los's Theorem' and every declaration and line number the finding cites is right: setoidPrestructure at 49, the ultraproduct «structure» at 74, funMap_cast at 77, term_realize_cast at 82, boundedFormula_realize_cast at 95, realize_formula_cast at 146, and the Los's Theorem docstring at 152 with sentence_realize immediately after. Worth noting that I checked these against a Mathlib tree at 30a58f79 rather than the pinned 082e2d3, so line agreement was not guaranteed and is stronger evidence than the finding needed. One mitigation the finding does not mention, which I record without changing the verdict: the same sentence begins 'integrate model-theory foundations from Mathlib where available', so the layer is not unaware of the library. But the explicit imperative that follows is 'Construct ultraproducts and prove the needed Los transfer theorem', and a worker following LD.0 as written would rebuild both. That makes this a wording error rather than an oversight, and the error is still real: medium stands, and the proposed rewrite — import the construction and the theorem, and add only the transfer interface on top — is the right correction. Scope of my judgement: model theory is not an area I have worked in this session, so this confirmation rests on reading the stage text and the pinned library rather than on independent judgement about whether the 'transfer interface this roadmap needs' is all that remains once Mathlib is imported.
